findings.claim: The attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` in every template. Consumers building for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework therefore get no `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` on any generated formatter or resolver. The requirement asks for ALL generated code to be decorated. The derived TFM criterion allows conditional emission only where the attribute does not exist. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` (class and struct targets) does exist in netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+, so this exclusion is a gap rather than a compile-safety need. The README hunk documents the gap instead of closing it.

It compiles the generator output with the preprocessor symbol NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK defined and asserts that every generated formatter and the resolver carry the attribute. findings.claim: No opt-out setting is added. The attribute is emitted unconditionally, with no GeneratorOptions, attribute property or MSBuild property to turn it off. Ledger L6 (area codegen-templates) records the answer "Add an opt-out setting", and no template consults any option before writing the attribute.
